knowledge:
- key_parameters: files=A named character vector or named BamFileList where names must be "treated" or "control" to describe the condition of each replicate ;; annotation=A GRangesList, GFF3File, or TxDb object containing genomic features ;; sequences=A FASTA file or XStringSet object containing genomic sequences ;; find.mod=Optional logical argument in Modifier constructors; if set to FALSE, prevents automatic search for modifications ;; minScore=A numeric threshold setting in Modifier objects (e.g., minScore = 0.5) used to filter modification calls ;; perTranscript=Logical argument in modifications(); if TRUE, returns coordinates relative to transcript boundaries instead of genomic coordinates ;; alias=A data.frame mapping transcript IDs to other names (e.g., gene names) for plotting ;; showSequenceData=Logical argument in plotData(); if TRUE, includes detailed pileup sequence data in the plot
- alternatives: RNAmodR.RiboMethSeq=Use this package's ModRiboMethSeq class to detect ribose methylations ;; RNAmodR.AlkAnilineSeq=Use this package's ModAlkAnilineSeq class to detect m7G and m3C modifications ;; Pseudo-Seq=An alternative high-throughput sequencing method for pseudouridine profiling mentioned in the literature
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to identify, map, and compare post-transcriptional RNA modifications (such as Inosine via A-to-G conversion) across single or multiple sample sets with replicate high-throughput sequencing data.
- pitfalls: BAM files must be explicitly named with "treated" or "control" conditions, or the package will fail to assign conditions ;; Using found modification sites directly as input for plotROC is strongly discouraged as it defeats the purpose of the performance test (circular logic) ;; For visualization with Gviz, naming chromosomes as chr1-chrN is recommended to avoid compatibility issues

workflows.name: single_sample_modification_detection
workflows.intent: Detect post-transcriptional RNA modifications (such as Inosine) in a single sample set with replicates.
workflows.stages: 1. Load annotation and sequence files ;; 2. Define named BAM file vector with "Treated" or "Control" conditions ;; 3. Create a SequenceData object (e.g., End5SequenceData) to load and parse BAM files ;; 4. Create a Modifier object (e.g., ModInosine) to automatically aggregate data and search for modifications ;; 5. Retrieve and adjust settings (e.g., minScore) of the Modifier object
workflows.code:
annotation <- GFF3File(RNAmodR.Data.example.gff3())
sequences <- RNAmodR.Data.example.fasta()
files <- c(Treated = RNAmodR.Data.example.bam.1(),
           Treated = RNAmodR.Data.example.bam.2(),
           Treated = RNAmodR.Data.example.bam.3())
seqdata <- End5SequenceData(files, annotation = annotation, 
                            sequences = sequences)
mi <- ModInosine(files, annotation = annotation, sequences = sequences)
settings(mi)
settings(mi,"minScore")
settings(mi) <- list(minScore = 0.5)
settings(mi,"minScore")

workflows.name: multi_sample_modification_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare post-transcriptional RNA modification profiles across multiple sample sets with replicates.
input: sample1_rep1.bam (BAM alignment for sample set 1 replicate 1)
sample1_rep2.bam (BAM alignment for sample set 1 replicate 2)
sample2_rep1.bam (BAM alignment for sample set 2 replicate 1)
sample2_rep2.bam (BAM alignment for sample set 2 replicate 2)
workflows.stages: 1. Load annotation and sequence files ;; 2. Define a named list of named character vectors representing BAM files for multiple sample sets ;; 3. Create a ModifierSet object (e.g., ModSetInosine) to process all sample sets in parallel ;; 4. Retrieve identified modifications using modifications() ;; 5. Compare modification scores across samples at specific coordinates using compareByCoord() ;; 6. Generate a TxDb object and alias data frame for transcript-to-gene mapping ;; 7. Visualize comparisons using heatmaps (plotCompareByCoord()) and transcript-level plots (plotData()) ;; 8. Evaluate performance using ROC curves (plotROC()) and retrieve read metadata statistics (stats())
workflows.code:
sequences <- RNAmodR.Data.example.AAS.fasta()
annotation <- GFF3File(RNAmodR.Data.example.AAS.gff3())
files <- list("SampleSet1" = c(treated = RNAmodR.Data.example.wt.1(),
                               treated = RNAmodR.Data.example.wt.2(),
                               treated = RNAmodR.Data.example.wt.3()),
              "SampleSet2" = c(treated = RNAmodR.Data.example.bud23.1(),
                               treated = RNAmodR.Data.example.bud23.2()),
              "SampleSet3" = c(treated = RNAmodR.Data.example.trm8.1(),
                               treated = RNAmodR.Data.example.trm8.2()))
msi <- ModSetInosine(files, annotation = annotation, sequences = sequences)
mod <- modifications(msi)
mod <- modifications(msi, perTranscript = TRUE)
mod <- modifications(msi)
coord <- unique(unlist(mod))
coord$score <- NULL
coord$sd <- NULL
compareByCoord(msi,coord)
txdb <- makeTxDbFromGFF(annotation)
alias <- data.frame(tx_id = names(id2name(txdb)),
                    name = id2name(txdb))
plotCompareByCoord(msi, coord, alias = alias)
plotCompareByCoord(msi[c(3,1,2)], coord, alias = alias, normalize = "SampleSet3",
                   perTranscript = TRUE)
plotData(msi, "2", from = 10L, to = 45L, alias = alias)
plotData(msi[1:2], "2", from = 10L, to = 45L, showSequenceData = TRUE, alias = alias)
plotROC(msi, coord)
stats <- stats(msi)
